# axionMultiPhysics

> Finite-element simulation for axion dark-matter detectors: lumped-element detectors (toroidal ABRACADABRA,
> solenoidal DMRadio and DMRadio-Core topologies, custom geometries) and, as beta modules, cavity haloscopes, SRF
> heterodyne cavities and dc SQUID readout chains. C++17 core on MFEM; Python API, `axmp` command line, three.js
> viewer and an MCP server.
> For lumped-element detectors it computes the signal coupling Psi = (1/I) int A_I . B_lab, the pickup inductance
> L_p, the scan figure of merit F = Psi^4/L_p^2 against the optimal-scan requirement F_req, fields, forces and a
> size/cost metric. Install: the 0.2.0 wheels follow on PyPI after the release; until `pip index versions axionmultiphysics` lists
> 0.2.0, `pip install axionmultiphysics` installs 0.1.0 (no 0.2.0 API), so install 0.2.0 from source
> (docs/guides/install.md). Wheels, once listed: `pip install "axionmultiphysics[mesh]"` (planned for Linux x86_64 and
> macOS, CPython 3.10-3.14; 0.2.0 was built and tested on Linux x86_64 only); the wheels have no 3D engine and no fluids module; an MPI source build adds both. Modules marked beta
> below are usable but less validated.
> Also beta: model documents (one physics-based input format for fluids, heat, electrochemistry and coupled physics:
> catalogue, validation, explain, patch, JSON Schema, named boundaries and bounded 2D meshes; not solved yet), the
> export to Geant4 (field maps, solids and GDML of axisymmetric and 3D designs) and particle transport
> (`axmp-transport`, a separate Geant4 program built with `-DAXMP_BUILD_TRANSPORT=ON`, driven by
> `axionmultiphysics.particles`).

Repository paths below are relative to the repository root. Documentation site:
https://bsafdi.github.io/axionMultiPhysics/

## Start here

## Design expressions
- Any numeric design field may be a string expression over `parameters` (functions sqrt exp log log10 sin cos
  tan asin acos atan atan2 abs min max pow; constants pi, e, mu0). Standard math precedence: `^` binds tighter
  than unary minus and is right-associative, so `-2^2` = -4, `exp(-z^2/(2*s^2))` is a Gaussian, `2^3^2` = 512,
  `2^-2` = 0.25 (as Python's `**`; not MATLAB's left-associative 2^3^2 = 64). Malformed numbers (`1.2.5`),
  out-of-range literals (`1e400`, `1e-310`), NaN arguments of min/max and nesting deeper than 1000 levels are
  errors. Grammar: docs/design_format.md.

## Errors
- Python: `axionmultiphysics.AxionMultiPhysicsError` (base `Exception`) has the attributes `code` (str, default ""),
  `where` (str, ""), `hint` (str, "") and `details` (dict or None); `str(e)` is the whole message. The CLI prints
  `ok`, `error`, `where`, `hint` and, only when the error has them, `code` and `details`; the MCP failure payload adds
  `code` and `details` the same way. `details` is a non-empty dict exactly when the CLI prints the key (details
  nested deeper than 64 levels are dropped everywhere). An error of `Design.solve(mpi_ranks=N)` has the four
  attributes from rank 0's JSON. The errors of an electromagnetic design carry no code (except
  `model.section_needs_physics`, below, and the three of an `arc` path: `geometry.arc_span` at `<path>/arc/angles` for
  angles that span more than one turn, 2 pi radians, with the angles in radians; `geometry.arc_degenerate` for a radius
  <= 0 (`<path>/arc/radius`) or an arc of 1e-7 m or less (`<path>/arc/angles`); and `geometry.arc_negative_r` at
  `<path>/arc` for an arc that reaches r < 0 in every electromagnetic design except xsec (planar designs on an imported mesh
  included) and in an axisymmetric model document; and also `mesh.tangled`: a 2D mesh of geometry order 2 with a
  tangled curved element (det J changing sign or inverted), refused where the mesh file is read, an imported
  `mesh.file` too; axmp-mesher itself repairs such a mesh (mesh info `high_order`) or refuses it, reported as `mesh
  generation failed: ...`, see "Curved elements in 2D" in docs/design_format.md); `axmp.physics(type=...)` with an
  unknown type raises with the code
  `physics.unknown_type`, and the refusals of a model document below carry theirs.
- Beta: the codes of the findings about a model document (a design with a `physics` section) are listed in
  docs/reference/error_codes.md, generated from `axionmultiphysics._core.error_codes()` (JSON text of a list of
  `{code, kinds, summary, status}` sorted by code; kinds are error, unavailable, deferred, warning). The grammar and
  the validation of model documents are in the C++ core; `axmp explain` / `Design.explain()` list one and `axmp patch` /
  `Design.patch()` edit one (RFC 6902, atomic, the result validated; a failed operation is `patch.operation_failed` with
  `where` `/<index>`); `explain` also lists the `time`, `save`, `initial_from` and `given` that a step writes, tagged `[written]`; `axmp boundaries` / `Design.boundaries()` list its named boundaries with the checks on them and `axmp mesh` / `axmp.mesh(d)` mesh a planar or axisymmetric one; none solves one yet. `axmp schema` covers both kinds of document (model sections `x-status: beta`). Most
  findings carry a code; the page says which do not. A `deferred` finding names a check that waits for the resolved
  boundaries or for an imported mesh file (`boundary.empty_selection`, `physics.boundary_uncovered`, ...).

- Beta: model documents at the entry points (a document with a top-level `physics` key). `axmp validate doc.json
  [--strict]` prints the report `{ok, name, parameters, errors, unavailable, deferred, warnings}` (each finding:
  `error`, `where`, `hint`, and `code` and `details` when it has them; most have a code); with an error `ok` is false,
  the first error's fields are also at the top level, exit 1; `--strict` does the same for the first `unavailable`
  finding when there is no error. `axmp resolve` prints the resolved geometry. `Design.validate(strict=False,
  all_errors=False)` and `_core.validate(design, strict=False, all_errors=False)` return the report and raise the
  first error (with strict, the first unavailable) unless all_errors. `axmp boundaries doc.json [--json] [--mesh] [-o DIR]
  [--mesher M]` and `Design.boundaries(mesh=False, all_errors=False)` print the table of the named boundaries (`symmetry`,
  `boundaries`, `edges`; no master numbers) after the full check (partition rule, empty selections, partial matches);
  `axmp mesh` / `_core.mesh` / `axmp.mesh(d, workdir=None, mesher=None)` mesh a planar or axisymmetric model document
  (`MeshedModel`, `.instance(domain=None)` -> `InstanceMesh` with `face_points(name=None, *, order, attribute=None)`); a
  geometry with no running mesher is the unavailable finding `build.requires_mesher`, a failed run `mesh.generation_failed`,
  an elliptical contour segment `model.shape_not_offered`. `axmp validate --mesher M` probes M. A `where` filter decides a straight edge exactly (a touching edge is no partial match) and a curved edge by its box, with an enclosure exception. `axmp mesh` first removes an earlier mesh in `-o`. `axmp.mesh` of a document with no geometry, a 3D one or one on an imported mesh raises `route.not_implemented`. `InstanceMesh.fluids_mesh()` / `MeshedModel.fluids_mesh(domain=None)` give a `fluids.Mesh` that copies the instance mesh (`Mesh.has_nodes`; MPI builds; elsewhere the unavailable code `build.requires_fluids`), and `InstanceMesh.chem_mesh(order=2)` / `MeshedModel.chem_mesh(domain=None, order=2)` a `chem.TriMesh` (`geometry_order`, `edge_nodes()`) for `chem.CurrentDistribution`; a field of order 1 on a mesh with nodes is a ValueError. Conditions go on `im.attributes[name]`, `im.remaining_attributes` and `im.axis_attributes`, never on master numbers. Solving (`axmp solve`, `_core.run_3d`, `Design.solve`, MCP
  `solve_design`/`sweep`) and meshing a 3D or imported-mesh model document refuse with `route.not_implemented`; the
  electromagnetic-only operations (`axmp sensitivities`, `_core.Model`/`Model3D`/`XsecModel`/`Fw2DModel`,
  `Design.gradient`/`optimize`, `axmp.optimize`/`global_optimize`, `sensitivity.optimize`, `convert.to_3d`, `axmp
  export-comsol`/`comsol.export_comsol` (a design, its `.json` or a run directory's `design.json`), MCP `make_3d`,
  `set_fullwave`, `set_hts`, `sensitivities`, `optimize_design`, `optimize_global`, `optimize`, `export_comsol`)
  refuse one with `model.em_only_operation`; both carry `details.operation` and `details.serves_model_documents`
  (`["validate", "resolve", "explain", "patch", "boundaries", "mesh"]`). Without `physics`, a top-level `domains`, `boundaries`, `reactions`, `couplings`,
  `study` or `outputs` is `model.section_needs_physics`. `axmp` and `axmp.load` refuse a model document that repeats a
  key in an object (`json.duplicate_key`, `where` = the JSON pointer of the second occurrence; a file read from a pipe
  too); an electromagnetic file keeps JSON's last value. `axmp export-comsol` prints an error that has a code as the
  MCP payload (`ok`, `error`, `where`, `hint`, `code`, `details`), any other error as before.

## Python API
- `axmp.templates()`, `axmp.template(name, **params)` -> `Design`; `Design.set(**params)`, `.validate()`, `.solve()` -> `Results`;
  `axmp.load(path)`, `axmp.schema()`, `Design.explain(json=False)` (beta, model documents), `Design.boundaries()` and `axmp.mesh(d)` (beta, model documents), `Design.patch(ops)` (beta; model documents and electromagnetic designs; the patched document has its keys sorted), `axmp.requirement(benchmark)`
- Beta: `axmp.physics(routes=False, type=None)` -> the physics catalogue of model documents (dict, schema
  `axionmultiphysics.physics_catalogue/1`): types, coupling terms, reserved instance ids and, with `routes=True`, the
  route table. No route is implemented yet (every row has `"implemented": false` and `"status": "not_implemented"`;
  `axmp physics --routes` prints "not implemented yet"). An unknown `type` raises `AxionMultiPhysicsError` whose hint
  lists the types.
- `Results`: `.Psi`, `.L_p`, `.F`, `.W`, `.g`, `.data` (the results document), `.benchmark(name)`, `.summary()`,
  `.reach(...)`, `.sample(r, z)` (lists of points), `.scene()`, `.png(view=...)`, `.export_html()`, `.write_vtu()`,
  `.show()` (Jupyter widget)
- `axmp.build_info()` -> what this build can do (`mpi`, `engine_3d`, `fluids`, `openmp`, `gpu_backend`, `device`).
  The wheels are sequential: `engine_3d` is False and a 3D design raises an error saying so.
- Sensitivities and optimization: `Results.sensitivities(params, objectives)` / `Design.gradient(...)` ->
  dJ/dp and d log J / d log p (adjoint on a morphed mesh; axisymmetric designs with linear materials);
  `axmp.objectives()` lists the quantities;
  `axmp.optimize(design, objective, params={name: (lo, hi)}, constraints=[...])` (scipy L-BFGS-B / SLSQP;
  `method="global"` for differential evolution, also `axmp.global_optimize`)
- `axionmultiphysics.scan`: `reach`, `psd`, `g_qcd`, `Q_axion_shm`; `axionmultiphysics.plots`: `reach`, `psd`,
  `section`, `force_distribution`. Every reach call returns a `"band"` dict echoing what was scanned (mass/frequency
  range, number of settings, allocation, live time, benchmark and the Q_axion/Theta/rho conventions)
- Readout circuit: `axionmultiphysics.circuit` (`series_readout`, `Readout.analyze/sweep/noise_curve/draw`,
  `Results.readout`) and its reduction to the scan inputs (Psi, L_eff, Q, T_eff, eta_A);
  `scan.finite_band(readout, f_min, f_max, ...)` plans a scan with the exact network noise N_V(omega) instead of that
  single pole and reports how far the reduction is off (docs/physics/readout_circuit.md Sec. 5.3,
  docs/validation/finite_band.md)
- `Results.forces`: winding `Fz_N` / hoop load, `Fz_self_N` and `Fz_excluding_self_N` (self-force removed),
  superconductor and iron Maxwell-pressure forces, `closure` (Newton's third law) and `distributions`
  (distributed surface traction / Lorentz density per body)
- Conductors: `axmp.conductors()`, `axmp.jc(conductor, B_perp, B_par, T)`; a winding's `conductor` gives
  `Results.conductors` (J_e and J_sc, peak |B| and the field angle to the tape, Jc at the worst point, load-line and
  temperature margins), also per benchmark and at the cost-optimal size
- HTS critical state: a design's `hts` section (regions, drive waveform, field_of_view) adds screening currents:
  `Results.hts` (distribution and profiles, SCIF, field quality, trapped flux, AC loss per cycle, Psi with the
  critical-state field) and `Results.hts_sample(r, z)`. Azimuthal screening currents only (poloidal static fields)
- Beyond MQS: a design's `fullwave` section (frequencies, boundary, modes) adds time-harmonic Maxwell results:
  `Results.fullwave` (Z(omega), L(omega), R_rad, Q_rad, Psi(omega), F(omega), eigenmodes);
  `scan.reach_fullwave(results, benchmark)` turns them into a beyond-MQS reach curve (Psi(omega), tuned-pole
  L_eff = L + 0.5 dL/dln(omega), Q = omega L_eff/(R_rad + R_material + omega L_p/Q_other)) against the MQS one;
  `scan.reach_dispersive` is the general frequency-dependent-detector scan. Local full-wave reach refuses unresolved
  slopes, optimized noise widths above 0.1*f, variations above 5% across that width, and bands outside the computed
  pre-resonance interval. Radiation has optional T_radiation_K; omitting it assumes the material bath temperature.
  Both L_reactive_H and L_eff_H are returned. The axisymmetric full-wave model is the uniform-feed (m = 0) limit.
  - Imposed backgrounds (beta in 3D): 3D sweeps couple a `background` (int curl E . A_bg inside and outside the domain sphere);
    axisymmetric TM sweeps include a grid background's exterior term with the same `Psi_background` rows,
    grid-coverage diagnostics and warnings. With a uniform background only the background's own exterior term is
    omitted (it diverges, with a warning). `Psi_exterior` is a different part of Psi in the two engines: compare
    totals (docs/physics/fullwave_background.md).
  - 3D full wave: current ports and multiport impedance matrices are validated; the prescribed source, perfectly
    matched layers, the imposed background, the error indicator, the Gauss-law guard, the adaptive sweep, the
    tree-cotree solve, 3D eigenmodes, closed RF-only models (`fullwave.rf_only`, `mesh.symmetry`, `mesh.remove_pec`)
    and the energy-matrix, field-export and reactive-load diagnostics are beta. `"status": "provisional"` is a fixed label of every 3D full-wave (and 2D imported-mesh) output,
    not a per-row verdict: acceptance is `validation_accepted`, `refused` and the warnings; a row or diagnostic that a
    solver or validation gate rejected carries `"status": "provisional_rejected"` and is kept for inspection only.
  - 3D adaptive sweep (beta): `fullwave.adaptive` {f_min_Hz, f_max_Hz, tolerance} fits a rational model (set-valued AAA,
    dZ/dw as Hermite data) to Z and Psi and solves where it is least certain until it holds to the tolerance over
    the band; `Results.fullwave_dense()` / `circuit.fullwave_dense(results)` give the dense curve,
    `circuit.fullwave_model(results)` evaluates the model; self_resonances are its poles with Q
    (docs/physics/adaptive_sweep.md).
  - 3D sweep rows carry perturbative surface losses per port from the `rf` surface-resistance models (beta):
    surface_Gamma, R_loss_ohm, the headline Q_loss_tuned = omega L_eff / R_loss, Q_loss = omega L / R_loss,
    R_loss_over_abs_X; Q_total is withheld where the solve's residual can move it by more than 1 %; rows whose Re Z
    the residual cannot resolve carry Re_Z_unresolved; `Results.fullwave_losses()` /
    `circuit.fullwave_losses(results, port)` give the columns (docs/physics/fullwave_surface_losses.md).
  - S/Y/Z parameters and Touchstone v1: `Results.write_touchstone(path, kind="S"|"Z"|"Y", z0=50, dense=False,
    surface_losses=False)` / `circuit.write_touchstone(results, path, ...)` / `axmp export-touchstone results.json`
    write `.sNp` in exp(+j omega t): the engine's exp(-i omega t) Z is conjugated. They report sigma_max(S)
    (passivity violations warned, never clipped) and ||Z - Z^T||/||Z||. CLI exit 0 ok, 3 not passive, 2 error.
    `axionmultiphysics.touchstone`: `read_touchstone`, `z_to_s`, `s_to_z`, `z_to_y`, `port_parameters`,
    `write_touchstone_data(..., convention=)` (docs/physics/touchstone.md).
- Electrostatics (axisymmetric and 3D): a design's `electrostatics` section (`boundary: open | grounded`) adds the
  Maxwell capacitance matrix and pairwise capacitances: `Results.electrostatics`, `Results.C_matrix`; a port pickup
  reports `Results.port_capacitance` (readout-gap capacitance and a lumped self-resonance estimate). In 3D the open
  boundary is an infinity-shell map; capacitances require h/p convergence. The matrix does not depend on the rank count
- Thin magnetic layers: a curve with `thickness` and a linear `mu_r` material is a mu-metal or iron shield in the
  axisymmetric magnetostatic engine (docs/physics/thin_magnetic_layer.md)
- Mechanics and heat conduction: a design's `mechanics` / `thermal` sections (material blocks `mechanical`,
  `thermal`) give `Results.mechanics`, `Results.thermal`, `Results.sample_mech(...)`; axisymmetric, 3D in MPI builds
- `axionmultiphysics.convert.to_3d(design)`: axisymmetric -> 3D design; `Design.solve()` on a 3D design returns
  `Results3D` (same numbers; `.sample(x, y, z)`, `.scene()` with a quarter cutaway, `.png()`, `.export_html()`,
  `.write_vtu()` -> ParaView). `Design.solve(mpi_ranks=N)` runs a 3D solve on N ranks
- Cavity haloscopes (beta): a design's `cavity` section (axisymmetric, `"symmetry": "xsec"` cross-sections, 3D) gives
  eigenmodes, form factors, geometry factors and Q0 (`Results.cavity_modes()`); `axionmultiphysics.cavity` (pillbox,
  coaxial and rod designs, tuning sweeps with mode tracking), `axionmultiphysics.cavity_xsec`,
  `axionmultiphysics.haloscope` (`scan_rate`, `beta_opt`, `g_limit_scan`, `preset_limit`),
  `axionmultiphysics.haloscope_presets` (published runs)
- SRF heterodyne cavities (beta): `axionmultiphysics.srf` (elliptical-cell geometry, mode pairs `cylinder_pair`, wall
  peaks), `axionmultiphysics.heterodyne` (`design_A`: volume, frequency, RF power and cost metric for a scan)
- dc SQUID readout chains (beta): `axionmultiphysics.squid.chain(preset)` (added noise, `.draw()`)
- Torsional dynamics (beta; m = 0, axisymmetric): `Results.torsion(nmodes=..., load=..., loads=[...],
  freqs_Hz=... | band={"f_Hz": [f0, f1], "n": N}, eta=...)` -> modes and the mobility Y = -i omega q of a load
  (e^{-i omega t}; Brownian S_q = 4 kB T Re Y/omega^2); `Results.torsion_band(f0, f1, loads=..., eta=..., length_m=L)`;
  `axionmultiphysics.torsion_waveguide.Tube(...).mobility(f, TubeLoad(...), eta)` (all-branch analytic mobility of an
  infinite tube; `Tube.finite_tube_mobility`, the finite tube) (docs/validation/torsion_highfreq.md)
- COMSOL: `axionmultiphysics.comsol` exports a design (mesh `.mphtxt`, Java model, STEP); `axmp.import_comsol(path)`
  (beta) imports a `.mph` model as a `Design` with an import report. No COMSOL installation is needed

## Beta modules without MCP tools
- `axionmultiphysics.fluids` (MPI builds only; not in the wheels): `Mesh` (`from_arrays`, `unit_square`, `annulus`),
  `solve_stokes` (Taylor-Hood, planar or axisymmetric with swirl), `Mesh3D` / `solve_stokes_3d` (distributed 3D),
  `solve_navier_stokes` (steady, planar or axisymmetric with swirl; `mhd={...}` with `geometry="planar25d"` for
  inductionless MHD on one rank), `solve_gls` (stabilized P1/P1, planar), `TransientNavierStokes` (BDF1/BDF2),
  `solve_heat` and `solve_boussinesq` (one rank). The nonlinear solvers gate their verdicts on the accuracy of the linear
  algebra: `solve_navier_stokes`, `TransientNavierStokes`, `solve_heat`, `solve_boussinesq` and `solve_gls` report
  `mass_lu_residual_max` (dual-norm mass solves, bound 1e-10; `solve_gls` also refuses a mass matrix it cannot
  factorize); `solve_navier_stokes` and `TransientNavierStokes` report `lu_residual_max` / history `lu_residual`
  (per-step direct solves, the final step bounded by `max(newton_rtol, 1e-11)`); `TransientNavierStokes.initialize`
  reports `projection_residual` / `projection_converged` (the backward error of the projection's saddle solve, per
  block: residual norm over the norm of the sizes of the block's terms; about 5e-17 for an accurate solve on any
  mesh, domain shape and length unit; gate `1e-13` at every `newton_rtol`; a failed projection returns False and
  makes `advance`, `step_trial`, `adapt` and `snapshot` raise; the error lists the attempts and names the other
  pressure treatment: the pinned pressure `nullspace="pin"` passed on the measured scaled or stretched domains where the
  mean-value multiplier was refused, but not everywhere: on `1e9 x 1e4` it is refused with Eigen's LU (`lu="eigen"`) and the multiplier passes with
  STRUMPACK; the default STRUMPACK chain accepts the pin there with MC64 job 2).
  Every direct solve walks a recorded chain of LU configurations, each accepted on the caller's own gate
  (`lu=` names the first; `lu_retry="auto"`, the default, or `"off"` for the first alone): diagnostics `lu_stage`
  (the configuration that produced the solution; `lu_backend` is its backend, `solver` the configured one),
  `lu_attempts` (one record per configuration tried), `lu_backward_error`, `projection_lu_attempts`, the counts of the
  call (`lu_solves`, `lu_escalated`, `lu_attempts_total`, `lu_failed`, ...; summed over the steps in
  `TransientNavierStokes.stats`), history `lu_attempts` / `lu_stage`; `lu_fallbacks`, `lu_fallback_backend` and
  `lu_matching_retry` are aliases for one release. `solve_stokes` and `solve_stokes_3d` carry none of the nonlinear
  gates;
  `quad_order_convection` whose rule does not integrate the convective form exactly is refused (exact degree, P2/Q2:
  5 planar / 6 axisymmetric on straight triangles, 6 / 7 on straight quadrilaterals, more on curved meshes; the
  default is the exact degree). Eigen's direct solver (`lu="eigen"`, and the fallback of a build without STRUMPACK; also
  that of `solve_stokes_3d`) runs on rank 0 alone and is limited by that rank's memory: STRUMPACK for large 3D (an
  out-of-memory factorization raises an error with the sizes and the remedies on every rank). Meshes come from arrays: no
  design document, mesher, CLI or viewer integration. Point evaluation needs one rank. With `strategy="newton"` only,
  a steady Navier-Stokes or MHD solve whose step stops reducing the residual at its measured round-off floor, still
  within a decade of `newton_rtol`, stops there and counts as converged, reporting `residual_floor` and
  `stopped_at_floor` (so `converged` bounds `relative_residual` by ten times `newton_rtol`; the stop accepts the
  iterate it fired on and can differ by a step between rank counts; `residual_floor_factor=0` switches that off, and
  the picard and ptc strategies, the time steps, GLS and Boussinesq ignore it; the accuracy gates above still apply to
  a floor stop, which then keeps `stopped_at_floor` and reports `converged = false`)
- `axionmultiphysics.transport.ScalarTransport` (MPI builds, one rank): the SUPG scalar-transport operator
- `axionmultiphysics.chem`: `CurrentDistribution` (primary and secondary current distribution, planar or axisymmetric;
  Butler-Volmer, Tafel or linearized kinetics), `CurrentDistribution3D` (MPI builds only), `PorousElectrode` (1D,
  linearized Butler-Volmer only), `Reaction`, `meshes`; `axionmultiphysics.chem.kinetics`: mechanisms, 0D reactors
  (`batch`, `cstr`, `semibatch`, `const_p_gas`, `adiabatic_liquid`, `pfr`), `equilibrium` (index-1 DAE) and `adaptive`
  (variable-step BDF2, ESDIRK3(2) or variable-order BDF). No species transport
- `axionmultiphysics.fieldmap` (field maps for particle transport): `Results.export_field_map(path, regions=None,
  tol=1e-4, merge=True, track_volumes=None, iterate_on_track_volumes=False, outside="refuse", max_patch_MB=512,
  max_total_MB=2048)` writes per-region patches of the recovered static field (kind 1: (B_r, B_z, B_phi) on an (r, z)
  grid; kind 3 from `Results3D`: (B_x, B_y, B_z)) with chord-RMS error control, format `axionmultiphysics.fieldmap/1`;
  `load(path)`, `write_map(path, patches)`, `FieldMap.evaluate(points, patch=name)` (Cartesian, m -> T; outside a
  patch's box by more than its `margin` (one level-0 spacing; nearer points are clamped onto the box)
  `fieldmap.outside_map` unless `outside="zero"`), `recovered_field`, `chord_error`, `decide`. Only superconducting
  sheets and thin magnetic layers split a region (an open one is refused); conductor curves are ignored. An unaccepted
  patch is written with `fieldmap.FieldMapWarning`; a chord that cannot be walked raises `fieldmap.chord_incomplete`; a patch with tangled curved elements (det J not of one sign)
  raises `fieldmap.tangled_mesh` (a second guard: a solve refuses a tangled mesh first, `mesh.tangled`). Beyond a curved interface inside the box the continuation holds only about one
  final-level cell (the margin applies at box faces).
  Seed spread of E up to 3-7 next to singular iron corners (reported). Codes `fieldmap.*` (docs/guides/field_maps.md)
- `axionmultiphysics.cavity_coupling`: a coaxial probe on the axis of an axisymmetric pillbox, TM0np modes only
  (`ProbePillbox`, `coupling_study`, `driven_coupling`, `to_haloscope_cavity`)
- `axionmultiphysics.solids` (beta; numpy only): `from_partition(partition, materials, region_materials,
  chord_tol_m=None)` turns an axisymmetric partition (the mesher's entity table with exact curves and face loops) into
  the solids list `axionmultiphysics.solids/1` (tube, torus, orb, generic polycone; notches at the axis filled, holes of
  the domain as vacuum daughters; arcs discretized once within min(1 um, 1e-5 x region size)) with a per-region Pappus
  volume and mass report (`particle.volume_deficit` above 1e-4); a layer thinner than the chord tolerance is refused
  (`particle.partition_invalid`: lower `chord_tol_m`; a discretized curve concave towards a solid it touches, and a face pinched at a point, are refused); `write(doc, path)`, `write_gdml(doc, path)` (17 significant
  digits, NIST materials referenced, never defined; names mapped to valid GDML names, `gdml_name`). `axmp-transport
  --geometry solids.json` builds it in Geant4 under the GDML names, runs the overlap check and prints the volumes,
  masses and materials as Geant4 built them. Codes `particle.*` (docs/guides/solids.md)
- `axionmultiphysics.particles` (beta; pure Python, drives `axmp-transport`, needs `AXMP_TRANSPORT` or the program
  next to `axmp`, else `build.requires_program`): `plan(workdir, *, solids, sources, outputs, events, fields=(),
  seed=1, chunk_events=1000, jobs=1, physics_list="FTFP_BERT" | "FTFP_BERT_EMZ" | "QGSP_BIC", production_cut_m=7e-4,
  integrator=None, outside="refuse" | "zero", quantum_eV=1e-3, stop=None, threads=1, program=None)`, `execute(workdir,
  workers=1)`, `merge`, `run` (all three), `extend(workdir, events=N2)` (bitwise equal to a direct run), `load`,
  `transport(design, results, *, sources, outputs, events, solids=..., field_map=None, map_tol=1e-4, ...)` (needs `solids=`: it does not run the partition export itself, `particle.partition_unavailable`;
  the solids document of `Design.export_gdml` can be passed), `resolve_materials(doc)` (a NIST
  composition at NIST's density becomes the NIST material itself, otherwise it carries NIST's I-value and state;
  `axmp-transport --nist`), `capabilities()`. One gun source (`particle`, `energy_eV` | `momentum_eV_c`, `at_m`,
  `direction` or "isotropic", `spot_sigma_m`); outputs: per-event `deposit`, `hit`, `primary`; aggregates `mean`,
  `std`, `quantile`, `fraction`, `count` (a `Measured` float with `stat_error`; Clopper-Pearson, exact zero-count 95 %
  limits, batch means over 20 batches), `histogram`, `tally` (exact 128-bit batch sums of quanta), `hits` (entry
  records). Fields: `uniform`, `current_loop`, `map` patches (per logical volume, pinned
  G4TDormandPrince45+G4IntegrationDriver, deltaIntersection <= 0.1 x the finest map spacing; regions beyond a patch's
  box refused with `particle.field_outside_map` unless `outside="zero"`). Merges the longest complete prefix of
  chunks (partial -> `events.partial`); a failed process is retried once; stop rules on prefixes from 20 chunks.
  Command line `python -m axionmultiphysics.particles {execute,merge,extend} WORKDIR` (exit status 5 when partial).
  One driver per workdir (an exclusive lock; `events.workdir_busy`); seeds in [0, 2^64); a map inside the workdir is
  named relative to it in job files, others by real path, and a map changed since the plan is refused
  (`events.field_map_changed`); a track Geant4 abandons as stuck is ended and counted (`abandoned_killed`,
  `abandoned_eV`, warning `particle.track_abandoned`). The world and voids end the
  domain only where a track really is (an interface between regions is never an exit). Statistical errors only.
  Codes `events.*`, `stat.*`, `particle.*`, `build.requires_program` (docs/guides/particles.md)

## MCP server
`axionmultiphysics-mcp` or `python -m axionmultiphysics.mcp_server` (stdio; workspace `$AXMP_WORKSPACE`, default
`./axmp_workspace`). Call `axionmultiphysics_guide` first. Tools:
- designs: `list_templates`, `create_design`, `get_design`, `put_design`, `set_parameters`, `list_designs`,
  `design_schema`, `make_3d`, `set_fullwave`, `set_hts`, `list_conductors`
- solving and looking: `solve_design`, `render_design`, `start_viewer`, `requirement`
- exploring: `sweep`, `sensitivities`, `list_objectives`, `optimize_design`, `optimize_global`, `optimize`
- jobs: `list_jobs`, `cancel_job`
- cavity haloscopes (beta): `cavity_presets`, `cavity_preset_limit`, `cavity_scan`, `create_cavity`
- SRF heterodyne (beta): `srf_design`, `srf_mode_pair`
- dc SQUID readout (beta): `squid_chain`, `squid_reach`
- COMSOL: `export_comsol`, `inspect_comsol` and `import_comsol` (the last two beta); Touchstone: `export_touchstone`
`solve_design`, `sweep`, `sensitivities`, `optimize_design`, `optimize_global` and `optimize` run in a worker
subprocess: they send MCP progress notifications, and `cancel_job(job_id)` (or the client's own cancellation) stops them.

## Command line
`axmp solve design.json [-o DIR] [--order P] [-v N] [--scene] [--vtu] [--save] [--no-self-force] [--force-samples N]
[--status-file F]`, `axmp sensitivities design.json [--param P]... [--objective Q]... [--method adjoint|fd_morph|fd_remesh]
[--step S] [--benchmark NAME]`, `axmp validate design.json`, `axmp mesh design.json [-o DIR]`, `axmp resolve
design.json`, `axmp schema`, `axmp physics [--json] [--type T] [--routes] [--all]` (beta: the physics catalogue,
no design file needed), `axmp requirement [--benchmark NAME]`, `axmp templates`,
`axmp template NAME [--set key=value ...]`,
`axmp render scene.json -o out.png [--view section|3d] [--quantity Q] [--log] [--theme dark]`,
`axmp export-comsol --help`, `axmp import-comsol model.mph --help`,
`axmp export-touchstone results.json [-o OUT.sNp] [--kind S|Z|Y] [--z0 50] [--dense] [--surface-losses]`.
